cards.text: The hail is over, and Pharaoh STILL won't let Israel go. So the LORD sends Moses, Israel's leader, back to Pharaoh. He tells Moses He has hardened the hearts of Pharaoh and his officials, so He can perform His miraculous signs among them.

cards.question: God says these signs are something Moses will tell his children and ___ so they all know He is the LORD.

cards.text: Moses and his brother Aaron walk back into the palace with a question from the LORD: "How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me?" Then the same request as always: let My people go, so they can worship Me.

cards.question: If Pharaoh refuses, the LORD says He will bring ___ into Pharaoh's territory tomorrow.
So many locusts that nobody can even see the ground. What will the locusts eat?

answers.text: Whatever is left after the hail
Only the grain by the Nile

cards.text: And they won't stay outside, friend. They'll fill Pharaoh's houses, his officials' houses, EVERY Egyptian house, something his fathers and grandfathers never saw. Then Moses just turns and walks out. No goodbye. No "any questions?" Gone.

cards.question: Moses has left the room. Who speaks up to Pharaoh next?
Pharaoh's officials tell him to let the people go so they can worship the LORD their God.

cards.text: Then they hit him with this: "Do you not yet realize that Egypt lies in ruins?" When your OWN staff stages an intervention, friend, it's bad. So Moses and Aaron get called back, and Pharaoh says, "Go, worship the LORD your God," and then... there's a catch.

cards.question: Pharaoh says go worship the LORD. What does he ask Moses and Aaron right after that?

answers.text: How many days they will be gone

cards.question: Pharaoh wants to know who is going to worship. Who does Moses say will go?

answers.text: Young and old with their flocks and herds
Only the elders and the priests
Only the families from the tribe of Levi

cards.text: Sons, daughters, flocks, herds, EVERYBODY. Moses says they must hold a feast to the LORD. I bet Pharaoh's eyebrows went up higher than mine, and friend, mine are BIG.

cards.question: Pharaoh agrees to let the Israelites' little ones go with them.
Pharaoh says that only the ___ may go and worship the LORD.

cards.text: And then Moses and Aaron are DRIVEN out of Pharaoh's presence. Getting tossed out of the room? Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer. I know the feeling. Then the LORD tells Moses to stretch out his hand over Egypt so the locusts can swarm in.

cards.question: Moses stretches out his staff over Egypt. What does the LORD send across the land all that day and night?

cards.text: By morning, that wind has brought the locusts, and they settle over ALL of Egypt. "Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be." That's not a swarm, friend. That's the all-time record.

cards.question: After the locusts cover the land, a few green plants are still left in Egypt.

cards.text: Egypt's covered black with locusts, and nothing green is left. So Pharaoh QUICKLY summons Moses and Aaron. The man who keeps saying no is suddenly in a big hurry.

cards.question: Pharaoh tells Moses and Aaron, "I have ___ against the LORD your God and against you."
Pharaoh admits his sin to Moses and Aaron. What does he ask them to do?

answers.text: Forgive him and appeal to the LORD
Leave Egypt before the next sunrise
Bring him an offering for the LORD

cards.text: He says forgive my sin "once more." ONCE MORE. Even Pharaoh knows this is a rerun. He asks them to pray that the LORD will remove "this death" from him, so Moses leaves and appeals to the LORD.

cards.question: Moses prays about the locusts. What does the LORD do with the wind?

answers.text: Changes it to a very strong west wind
Stops it completely for a whole day
Sends it south toward the desert

cards.question: After the wind blows the locusts into the Red Sea, a few locusts stay behind in Egypt.

cards.text: Not one locust left. The cleanest Egypt has been in WEEKS. And then... the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
So the LORD tells Moses to stretch out his hand toward heaven, so darkness will spread over Egypt. And not just any darkness: "a palpable darkness." Darkness you can FEEL, friend.

cards.question: Moses stretches out his hand, and total darkness covers all of Egypt. How long does it last?

cards.text: Three days. No one can see anyone else, and no one leaves his place. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, and even I say that's dark.

cards.question: While Egypt is in total darkness, the Israelites' homes are dark too.

cards.text: Pharaoh summons Moses again and says, "Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you." Look at him, negotiating. Every plague he gives up a little more. But he's still holding something back.

cards.question: Pharaoh says the little ones can go this time. What does he say must stay behind?

cards.text: Moses doesn't take the deal. He says Pharaoh must ALSO give them sacrifices and burnt offerings for the LORD. Pharaoh came in trying to keep the animals, and now Moses is asking him to chip in more.

cards.question: Moses says not a hoof will be left behind. Why does he say all the livestock must go with them?

answers.text: They'll need some of them to worship the LORD
The herds would wander off without them
The animals are too weak to stay behind

cards.question: Moses tells Pharaoh they already know how they will worship the LORD before they leave.

cards.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go. Then Pharaoh says, "Depart from me!" and tells Moses to make sure he never sees Pharaoh's face again.

cards.question: Pharaoh warns that on the day Moses sees his face again, Moses will ___.
Pharaoh has just told Moses to never see his face again. How does Moses answer?

answers.text: He agrees he'll never see Pharaoh's face again
He begs Pharaoh for one more meeting
He asks Aaron to go back in his place

cards.text: "As you say," Moses replied, "I will never see your face again." Calm. Quiet. Done. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend. But this story is NOT over.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 2 quotes "I have ___ against the LORD your God and against you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The true or false statement 'Pharaoh agrees to let the Israelites' little ones go with them' is marked False, but in Exodus 10:24 Pharaoh does say 'Even your little ones may go with you.' The wrong pick (True) is true elsewhere in the passage, so a baker could argue it. Tie the statement to this moment, for example by asking whether Pharaoh agrees to let only the men go, or by naming this first offer.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the stock phrase 'children and ___' (grandchildren). That tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. Card 1 also gives no setup about telling future generations. The question also says only Moses will tell, but the text says 'you may tell… so that all of you may know,' which leaves open who is telling.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card retells Exodus 10:15 ('covered black with locusts, and nothing green is left') but cites only Exodus 10:16. It also restates what stop 1 card 18 already covered, which makes it a recap.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'Not one locust left' is from Exodus 10:19, but the card cites only Exodus 10:20. It also repeats what card 6 just answered, which makes it a recap. 'The cleanest Egypt has been in WEEKS' adds a time span the text never gives. 'Cleanest' also clashes with a land stripped bare.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'In WEEKS' adds a time frame to the plagues that the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'Darkness you can FEEL, friend' spends card words defining 'palpable.' The dictionary pop-up should handle that.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: 'Every plague he gives up a little more' isn't true. Pharaoh doesn't give ground after every plague (for example, no concession after the hail in Exodus 9:34-35). The claim stretches the pattern beyond the text.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: 'Even Pharaoh knows this is a rerun' states what Pharaoh knows as fact. If it stays, mark it as Papa Dorin's own guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: 'Calm. Quiet.' describes how Moses spoke as fact, but the text gives no tone. Mark it as a guess or cut it.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The joke compares being driven out of Pharaoh's presence to the junk drawer. But Papa Dorin wasn't tossed out. He was put away into the drawer ('He wasn't thrown away'). The actions don't match, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: the officials' 'Egypt lies in ruins' line plus a joke, Moses and Aaron being brought back, and Pharaoh's 'Go, worship' offer with its catch. Split it.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The opening card uses context from the passage before ('The hail is over, and Pharaoh STILL won't let Israel go,' Exodus 9:33-35) but cites only Exodus 10:1. The docs say outside facts carry their reference and a card cites exactly what it uses. They don't say whether a card's single 'verses' field may reach outside the passage (for example, 'Exodus 9:33-10:1').
findings.question: When the opening card gives context from the passage before, how should it be cited: widen the card's verses range outside the passage, add a separate reference, or leave the context uncited?
